newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ FCL's Fletcher outlines woods strategy.
newsitem.headline: NZ FCL's Fletcher outlines woods strategy.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Ltd Chief Executive Hugh Fletcher said on Thursday the company remained optimistic solid wood would remain one of its more favourably placed products, "but we do not underestimate the challenges".

Fletcher told the company's annual meeting that a collapse in pulp and paper prices had been a dominant feature of the past year, cutting FCL Paper's operating cashflow to NZ$104 million in the six months to June 1996 from $522 million in the half-year to December 1995.
Radiata log prices had weakened further throughout the year, moving for the first time in four years below the 20-year long-term trend line.

In softwoods, Fletcher said the recent acquisition of formerly state-owned Forestry Corporation by an FCL-led consortium was central to the company's focus on its North Island radiata pine plantations.

The proposal for Fletcher Challenge Forest Division to take over the solid wood processing facilities of the Building Division, which was being voted on at the meeting, was also part of this strategy.

Fletcher noted the company was also building new processing plants, including a NZ$11 million laminating plant now being commissioned at Kawerau and a $13 million plant under construction at the Taupo sawmill.

Woodchips would go to the Paper Division's $120 million thermo mechanical pulp mill now under construction at Kawerau. This would reduce the cost of producing newsprint by $100/tonne or 15 percent. It would enable an additional 75,000 tonnes per annum of kraft pulp worth $57 million to be exported, Fletcher said.
